name: B10-0278/2026 (ECR) – Implementation of the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (UWWTD) and risks to the security of supply of medicines
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the implementation of the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (UWWTD) and risks to the security of supply of medicines
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to pause two parts of the EU's wastewater clean-up law for two years. One part requires extra treatment to remove medicine and cosmetic residues from wastewater. The other makes drug and cosmetics companies pay most of the cost. The Parliament wants a new independent study first, because it fears the costs are much higher than expected and could make medicines more expensive or harder to find.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament asks the Commission to propose a two-year pause and a new cost study.
- **Who it affects:** Drug makers, cosmetics firms, water companies, and patients across the EU.
- **What happens next:** The Commission decides whether to propose the pause; Parliament also wants regular checks on medicine shortages.
